spots.name: Union Station
spots.summary: Denver Union Station is the main railway station and central transportation hub in Denver, Colorado. It is located at 17th and Wynkoop Streets in the present-day LoDo district and includes the historic station house, a modern open-air train shed, a 22-gate underground bus station, and light rail station.

spots.name: Denver Art Museum
spots.summary: The Denver Art Museum (DAM) is an art museum located in the Civic Center of Denver, Colorado. With an encyclopedic collection of more than 70,000 diverse works from across the centuries and world, the DAM is one of the largest art museums between the West Coast and Chicago.

spots.name: Colorado State Capitol

hours.note: Closed Sat, Sun

spots.summary: The Colorado State Capitol Building, located at 200 East Colfax Avenue in Denver, Colorado, United States, is the home of the Colorado General Assembly and the offices of the Governor of Colorado, Lieutenant Governor of Colorado, and the Colorado State Treasurer.

spots.name: Cathedral Basilica of the Immaculate Conception

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Cathedral Basilica of the Immaculate Conception is the cathedral of the Archdiocese of Denver of the Roman Catholic Church. It is located at the corner of Logan Street and Colfax Avenue in the North Capitol Hill neighborhood of central Denver. It has a seating capacity of 895 persons.
spots.wikipediaTitle: Cathedral Basilica of the Immaculate Conception (Denver)

spots.name: Republic Plaza

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Republic Plaza is a skyscraper in Denver, Colorado. Rising 714 feet, the building currently stands as the tallest building in the city of Denver and the entire Rocky Mountain region of the United States. It was built in 1984, and contains 56 floors, the majority of which are used as office space.

spots.name: Denver Mint

hours.note: Closed Fri, Sat, Sun

spots.summary: The Denver Mint is a branch of the United States Mint that struck its first coins on February 1, 1906. The mint is still operating and producing coins for circulation, as well as mint sets and commemorative coins. Coins produced at the Denver Mint bear a D mint mark.

spots.name: Elitch Gardens Theme Park
spots.summary: Elitch Gardens Theme & Water Park, colloquially known as Elitch's, is an amusement park in Denver, Colorado. It is owned by KSE Radio Ventures, LLC and operated by Premier Parks, LLC. It is open April through October.

spots.name: Denver Museum of Nature and Science
spots.summary: The Denver Museum of Nature & Science is a municipal natural history and science museum in Denver, Colorado. It is a resource for informal science education in the Rocky Mountain region.
spots.wikipediaTitle: Denver Museum of Nature and Science

spots.name: Wings Over the Rockies Air and Space Museum
spots.summary: The Wings Over the Rockies Air and Space Museum (WOTR) is located on the former Lowry Air Force Base in Denver, Colorado, United States. The museum preserves the history of Lowry AFB's operations from 1938 to 1994 in its collections, archives, and research library.
spots.wikipediaTitle: Wings Over the Rockies Air and Space Museum

spots.name: Denver Civic Center
spots.summary: The Denver Civic Center is a civic center that includes two parks surrounded by government and cultural buildings and spaces in central Denver, Colorado, on the south side of Downtown Denver. Much of the area is a historic district which was listed on the National Register of Historic Places in 1974.

spots.name: Denver Botanic Gardens
spots.summary: The Denver Botanic Gardens is a public botanical garden located in the Cheesman Park neighborhood of Denver, Colorado. The 23-acre (93,000 m2) park contains a conservatory, a variety of theme gardens and a sunken amphitheater, which hosts various concerts in the summer.

spots.name: Empower Field at Mile High
spots.summary: Empower Field at Mile High is an American football stadium in the western United States, located in Denver, Colorado. Opened 25 years ago in 2001, its primary tenant is the Denver Broncos of the National Football League (NFL), and it replaced the Broncos' original home, Mile High Stadium.

spots.name: Daniels & Fisher Tower
spots.summary: The Daniels & Fisher Tower is a distinctive historic landmark located in Denver, Colorado.

photo.author: The original uploader was MrB at English Wikipedia.

spots.name: Denver Public Library

hours.note: Closed Sun; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Denver Public Library is the public library system of the City and County of Denver, Colorado, United States. The system includes Denver Central Library, located in the Golden Triangle district of Downtown Denver, as well as 28 branch locations and two bookmobiles.

spots.name: U.S. Bank Tower

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The U.S. Bank Tower is a 389 ft (119m) tall office skyscraper in Denver, Colorado. It was completed in 1975 and has 26 floors. Minoru Yamasaki & Associates designed the building and it is currently the 22nd tallest in Denver.

spots.name: City Park
spots.summary: City Park is an urban park and neighborhood in Denver, Colorado. The park is 330 acres (1.3 km2) and is located in east-central Denver. The park contains the Denver Zoo, the Denver Museum of Nature and Science, Ferril and Duck Lakes, and a boathouse.

spots.name: Civil War Monument
spots.summary: The Civil War Monument is a statue of a Civil War cavalryman by Jack Howland that was originally installed outside the Colorado State Capitol in Denver. The memorial is also known as the Civil War Memorial, Soldier's Monument, and Civil War Soldier.

spots.name: Coors Field
spots.summary: Coors Field is a baseball stadium in downtown Denver, Colorado, United States. It is the ballpark of Major League Baseball's Colorado Rockies. Opened in 1995, the park is located in Denver's Lower Downtown neighborhood, two blocks from Union Station. The stadium has a capacity of 50,144 people for baseball.

spots.name: Larimer Square
spots.summary: Larimer Square is a historic district located along Larimer Street in downtown Denver, Colorado. It is recognized as Denver’s oldest surviving commercial district and was designated the city’s first historic district in 1971.

spots.name: Lao Tzu
spots.summary: Lao Tzu is a 1996 sculpture by Mark di Suvero, previously installed at Denver's Acoma Plaza at West 13th Avenue, in the U.S. state of Colorado.

spots.name: The Closing Era
spots.summary: The Closing Era is a bronze sculpture of a Native American hunter standing over a dying bison, installed on the East side of the Colorado State Capitol in Denver.

spots.name: Confluence Park
spots.summary: Confluence Park is an urban park encompassing the confluence of Cherry Creek and the South Platte River in Denver's Lower Downtown (LoDo), a bustling district of 19th-century brick warehouses and storefronts that has been redeveloped since the late 1980s.

spots.name: Cathedral of St. John in the Wilderness

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Saint John's Cathedral in Denver, Colorado, United States is the seat of the bishop and the cathedral of the Episcopal Diocese of Colorado and part of the Episcopal Church in the United States.
spots.wikipediaTitle: Cathedral of St. John in the Wilderness

spots.name: Evans Memorial Chapel

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Evans Memorial Chapel is an historic chapel on the campus of the University of Denver in Colorado. It is the oldest continuously-used building for religious purposes in Denver. Completed in 1878, the Evans Memorial Chapel was built with patronage by John Evans in honor of his daughter Josephine.

spots.name: Denver Athletic Club
spots.summary: The Denver Athletic Club, founded in 1884, is a private athletic and social club that is member-owned. Located in Downtown Denver, Colorado, United States. Residing in the historical 1325 Glenarm Place near the Colorado Convention Center, The DAC was added to the U.S. National Register of Historic Places in 1979.

spots.name: Spire

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Spire is a high-rise building containing 496 condominium homes in Denver, Colorado, in the United States. Standing at 147.2 metres (483 ft) with 42 floors, Spire is the tenth tallest building in Denver and was designed by architecture firm RNL Design.

spots.name: Pioneer Fountain
spots.summary: Pioneer Fountain, also known as Pioneer Monument, is a fountain and sculpture by Frederick William MacMonnies, installed in Denver, Colorado, United States.

spots.name: Clyfford Still Museum

hours.note: Closed Mon

spots.summary: The Clyfford Still Museum is an art museum in Denver, Colorado. The museum's collection includes 3,125 works by abstract expressionist Clyfford Still (1904–1980), which represents 93 percent of the artist's lifetime output and complete archives.

spots.name: Kirkland Museum of Fine & Decorative Art

hours.note: Closed Mon

spots.summary: Kirkland Museum of Fine & Decorative Art is an art museum in Denver, Colorado, United States. The museum houses three principal collections and includes the original studio and art school building of artist Vance Kirkland (1904–1981).
spots.wikipediaTitle: Kirkland Museum of Fine & Decorative Art

spots.name: Museum of Contemporary Art Denver

hours.note: Closed Mon

spots.summary: The Museum of Contemporary Art, in Denver, Colorado, was founded in 1996 as the first dedicated home for contemporary art in the city of Denver. For seven years, MCA Denver occupied a renovated fish market in Sakura Square in lower downtown Denver.

spots.name: History Colorado Center
spots.summary: The History Colorado Center is a museum in Denver, Colorado, US, dedicated to the history of the state of Colorado. Construction on the $111 million building started on August 19, 2009.

spots.name: Hyatt Regency Denver at the Colorado Convention Center

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Hyatt Regency Denver at the Colorado Convention Center is a 489 ft (149 m) tall skyscraper in Denver, Colorado, United States. It was constructed from 2003 to 2005 and has 38 floors. It is the 8th tallest building in Denver. It is currently owned by Plant Holdings NA, Inc. and leased to Hyatt Corporation.
spots.wikipediaTitle: Hyatt Regency Denver at the Colorado Convention Center

spots.name: Denver Millennium Bridge
spots.summary: The Denver Millennium Bridge is the world's first cable-stayed bridge using post-tensioned structural construction. Located near LoDo, in Riverfront Park, it connects the 16th Street Mall with the Commons Park in the Central Platte Valley District of the Union Station neighborhood.

spots.name: Ellie Caulkins Opera House
spots.summary: The Ellie Caulkins Opera House is located in Denver, Colorado as part of the large Denver Performing Arts Complex. It seats 2,225. The Caulkins family pledged $7 million towards the enhancement of the lyric opera house and adjacent public spaces which were constructed inside of the Newton Auditorium.

spots.name: Voorhies Memorial
spots.summary: The Voorhies Memorial is located in the Denver Civic Center, in the U.S. state of Colorado. It was designed by Fisher & Fisher and completed in 1919. It has a triumphal arch and curved supporting wings with roofed columns, as well as murals by Allen Tupper True.

spots.name: One Tabor Center

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: One Tabor Center is a 408 feet (124 m) tall skyscraper in Denver, Colorado. The building was completed in 1984 and has 30 floors. It is the 15th tallest building in Denver.

spots.name: Bronco Buster
spots.summary: Bronco Buster is a 1920 statue by Alexander Phimister Proctor, installed in Denver, Colorado, United States.

spots.name: First Baptist Church of Denver

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: First Baptist Church of Denver is an historic church at 230 E. 14th Avenue-1373 Grant Street in Denver, Colorado. First Baptist Church of Denver ("FBCD") was formally organized in 1864, six years after the city's founding.

spots.name: On the War Trail
spots.summary: On the War Trail is a 1922 statue by Alexander Phimister Proctor, installed outside the Colorado State Capitol in Civic Center Park, Denver, United States. The bronze sculpture depicts a Native American riding on a horse and carrying a spear.

spots.name: 1600 Glenarm Place

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: 1600 Glenarm Place is a 384 ft (117m) tall skyscraper in Denver, Colorado. Originally constructed in 1967 as the Security Life Building - it has since been converted into a multi-tenant luxury apartment complex. On the top floor of this building many years ago; there was a restaurant called Top Of The Rockies.

spots.name: Brooks Tower

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Brooks Tower is a 42-story, 420-foot residential skyscraper at 1020 15th Street in downtown Denver, Colorado, completed in 1968. It was designed by Cleveland architect Max Ratner and developed by the Brooks Realty and Construction Company.

spots.name: Colorado History Museum

hours.note: Closed Mon; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Colorado History Museum was a museum in Denver, Colorado, United States, dedicated to the history of Colorado. It was at 1300 Broadway in Denver from 1976 to 2010, and was administered by the Colorado Historical Society, now known as History Colorado.

spots.name: Mile High Stadium
spots.summary: Mile High Stadium was an outdoor multi-purpose stadium located in Denver, Colorado, from 1948 to 2002.

spots.name: 621 17th Street

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: 621 17th Street, formerly known as the First Interstate Tower South, is a high-rise building in Denver, Colorado, United States. The building was completed in 1957, and rises 28 floors and 385 feet (117 m) in height. The building stands as the 20th-tallest building in Denver and Colorado.

spots.name: Denver Firefighters Museum

hours.note: Closed Mon, Sun

spots.summary: The Denver Firefighters Museum is a museum in downtown Denver, Colorado, United States. A nonprofit institution 501 (C) (3), it consists of an 11,000-square-foot (1,000 m2) facility housing four galleries that explore the history of firefighting in Denver.

spots.name: Denver Central Library
spots.summary: The Denver Central Library is the flagship building of the Denver Public Library System. It is located within Downtown Denver's Golden Triangle neighborhood and sits on the south side of Colorado's 16th Street Mall, adjacent to the Denver Art Museum. The postmodern building was designed by architect Michael Graves.

spots.name: Telephone Building
spots.summary: The Mountain States Telephone Building is a historic building located at 931 14th Street in Denver, Colorado, United States. It was listed on the National Register of Historic Places on January 26, 2005.

spots.name: Colorado National Bank Building
spots.summary: Located in the Downtown Denver Historic District, the Colorado National Bank Building was designed by Denver architects William E. and Arthur A. Fisher and constructed in 1915. It is located at 918 17th Street, the intersection of 17th and Champa Streets.

photo.author: Jeffrey Beall from Denver, Colorado, USA

spots.name: Liberty Bell
spots.summary: The Liberty Bell in Denver is a replica of the original Liberty Bell, installed outside the Colorado State Capitol. The bell was 1 of 53 replicas cast in France in 1950.

spots.name: Dominion Plaza

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Dominion Towers is an office complex in Denver, Colorado. It consists of two adjoining towers, and was built in 1982. The taller one, Dominion Towers South, is 384 feet (117 m) tall and has 28 floors. The buildings have pink granite facades and blue-tinted windows.

spots.name: 1999 Broadway

spots.summary: 1999 Broadway is a 46-story high-rise office building in the city of Denver, Colorado. The building was designed by Curtis W. Fentress, FAIA, RIBA of Fentress Architects and its construction was completed in 1985. It stands at a height of 548 ft (166m), making it the 6th tallest building in Denver.

spots.name: Sakura Square
spots.summary: Sakura Square is a small plaza located on the north/east side of the intersection of 19th Street and Larimer Street in Denver, Colorado. The square contains busts of Ralph L.

spots.name: Big Sweep
spots.summary: Big Sweep is a sculpture by Claes Oldenburg and Coosje van Bruggen, installed in Denver, Colorado, United States. It depicts a broom and dustpan, and has been outside the Denver Art Museum since 2006.

spots.name: 633 17th Street

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: 633 17th Street, formerly known as the First Interstate Tower North, is a high-rise building in Denver, Colorado. The building was completed in 1974, and rises 32 floors and 434 feet (132 m) in height. The building stands as the twelfth-tallest building in Denver and Colorado.

spots.name: Masonic Temple Building
spots.summary: The Masonic Temple Building in Denver, Colorado is a Richardsonian Romanesque style building from 1889, designed by Frank E. Edbrooke. It was listed on the National Register of Historic Places in 1977.

spots.name: Boettcher Concert Hall
spots.summary: Boettcher Concert Hall is a concert hall in Denver, Colorado and is home to the Colorado Symphony. It is named after Colorado native and philanthropist Claude K. Boettcher.

spots.name: 1670 Broadway

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: 1670 Broadway, formerly Amoco Tower, is a 448 feet (137 m) tall skyscraper in Denver, Colorado. It was completed in 1980 and has 36 floors. Kohn Pedersen Fox Associates PC designed the building and it is the 11th tallest skyscraper in Denver.

spots.name: Sherman Street Event Center
spots.summary: The Mosque of the El Jebel Shrine, which has also been known as the Rocky Mountain Consistory, and as the Scottish Rite Temple is a historic building in the North Capitol Hill neighborhood of downtown Denver. It was for a period known as Sherman Street Event Center

spots.name: American Museum of Western Art – The Anschutz Collection

hours.note: Closed Tue, Thu, Sat, Sun

spots.summary: The American Museum of Western Art – The Anschutz Collection is a non-profit museum located in Denver, Colorado. Founded in 2010, it is the permanent home for The Anschutz Collection, a formerly private collection of paintings that surveys the art of the American West from the early 19th century to the present.
